notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); the hardware backend was never opened and nothing ran on a glove. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card's helper PythonObjectDriver is not used; the driver is a direct decorated Driver because OpenCyberGlove.get_data(hand_type) returns a GloveSensorData packet (open_cyber_glove/sdk.py:47-70, open_cyber_glove/glove.py:23-41) and the family's declarative read cannot pass the hand argument or select packet fields. Covered: the 19 tensile values, accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetometer, temperature and packet timestamp as read state; cap.sensing.read.v1 capture with the class example fields=['temperature'] and an all-channel default; the native stop OpenCyberGlove.stop as the latched e-stop; a native read failure and a failing native stop are raised, not swallowed. The hand option defaults to left; a deployment with a right glove must set hand=right. Not covered: cap.device.calibrate.v1 is not exposed because Glove.calibrate and advanced_calibrate wait on input() at pose prompts (glove.py:264-284, 303-325); get_angles is not exposed because the linear path raises NotImplementedError and the model path needs an ONNX model (glove.py:376-397, sdk.py:72-97). The README marks acc_data, gyro_data and mag_data 'To be added' (README.md:115-117); the driver exposes the fields the SDK parses but does not claim the vendor delivers meaningful IMU values yet. The vendor range statements differ (README.md:114 says 0-16384; docs/setup/user_guide_en.md:32 says 0-16380); the driver records both as facts, declares no Limit (there is no numeric write or invoke input) and does not clamp. Hardware deployment needs the card's pip install . (the upstream imports torch, open3d, onnxruntime and matplotlib at import time) plus the hand and port options; native.py refuses a missing port for the selected hand. The e-stop stops the SDK readers; stop_reader neither closes the serial port nor clears the packet queue (glove.py:94-137), there is no separate resume, and a reset does not restart acquisition: the held last packet is returned with acquisition='stopped' and the deployment must reopen the device. Reopening the same serial port was not tested. The fake is an analytic F0 stand-in with fixed placeholder packet values (only the timestamp advances), no serial transport, no 120 Hz pacing, no CRC or tensile range checks and no port/availability check; it is not a recording and its values are not facts. The gate's only warning is G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE: no actuating capability has a numeric limit to probe, so the suite awards CL2, not a full CL3; every other CL3 test passed. This package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json authored_by kind model, reviewed_by null).

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the direct Driver over OpenCyberGlove (open_cyber_glove/sdk.py:7) that the readiness evidence proposed for this reroute (a glove on a framed binary serial protocol, not a tag device): the glove is input-only (docs/safety_en.md:25), R1 is the card floor, no write or limit exists, the e-stop is the SDK's own stop (sdk.py:39-45, which joins each reader thread), and after a stop the driver returns the held last packet with acquisition 'stopped' instead of calling the getter of a stopped reader. Every fact was read against its lines; one added a clause from outside its range ('the serial read timeout is one second' on glove.py:127-137; the timeout is on 111) and now states the join without a timeout that the range shows, and the get_raw_data fact now says that it waits without a timeout (212-222). The reviewer changed driver.py and facts.md and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json; the gate and collect.py --strict pass with the digest unchanged (sha256:ae8bebad60c93e7d7a5d62275ed7068967f74cd7293d92a1f7e9a4731a9ad313). For the human reviewer: Upstream get_data blocks without a timeout until a packet is queued (glove.py:215-216): with a silent or unplugged glove, setup and every fresh read wait until the runtime's deadline while the native thread keeps polling, and a read in flight when the e-stop stops the readers can wait forever; the fake never blocks. The IMU floats are raw packet values that the README marks 'To be added' (README.md:115-117), and a non-finite value would fail the whole state read. Importing the upstream package loads torch and onnxruntime and configures root logging (glove.py:11-21, sdk.py:5).
